# Calls, speakers and model routing

## Google Voice

Open Interviews → Live interview and choose Google Voice as the call service.
Open Voice in a separate browser tab and place/answer the call there. Obtain
permission from everyone before capture. Start the session, choose that browser
tab and check Share tab audio. Allow microphone capture separately. Headphones
reduce echo. Confirm both level meters move when their respective person speaks.
A desktop browser supporting tab-audio capture is required; permission prompts
and support differ by browser/OS. Google Voice browser calling support is not
the same as tab-audio capture support. Phone-only calls are not captured.

This integration does not log into Google on your behalf, sync your account,
read private call APIs, dial automatically, answer an incoming phone call, or
send synthesized speech. Suggested replies appear on screen. The browser picker
includes a video track because it is required for tab sharing, but this path only
processes/transmits audio. Stop sharing or End stops this app's capture, including
the microphone; hang up separately in Google Voice. Permission cancellation and
late grants release their own tracks without interfering with a newer session.

## Speaker attribution

Finalized ASR messages are split at word-level speaker changes. Interims remain
one replaceable hypothesis so repeated ASR revisions cannot append duplicate
speaker turns. If formatted text cannot be aligned safely, the full text stays
intact and mixed speech is unknown instead of silently assigned to speaker zero.
Call and microphone speaker IDs are separate namespaces. The Names disclosure
lets the user assign names/roles to observed finalized voices; these are assertions
by the user, not biometric identification. Names flow through visible transcript,
answer context, text export, and the saved account-local feedback transcript.
Only the current session retains this speaker map. Source arrival order is
approximate, not synchronized speaker timing. Echo and overlapping voices can
still cause mistakes. Review before relying on the transcript.

## Model settings

Auto selects the configured tier for a question's mode. Fast selects the fast
conversational tier; Quality selects the smart tier. Output format (keywords,
concise, detailed) is independent. Image requests retain the smart tier. Repository
specialists and vision use their own per-role config rather than this dropdown.
These names describe intent, not measured guarantees. Existing purpose-specific
benchmarks remain the gate for labeling a model winner.

OpenRouter routing is explicit: prefix a server-configured ID with
`openrouter/provider/model`. Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` only in the hosting secret
store. Never reuse a secret exposed in chat; rotate it first. No new secret is
included in this release. An OpenRouter key alone does not change default routing.
Set `COPILOT_MODEL_FAST` / `COPILOT_MODEL_SMART` or per-role repository overrides.
Keys and endpoints are not accepted from client request bodies. Upstream errors,
truncated completions and missing completion events fail visibly. Repository
specialists do not silently substitute a reviewer. OpenRouter cost is marked
unknown in generic telemetry until actual provider billing is available.

Manual repository benchmarks can compare prefixed OpenRouter IDs, using the same
production adapter; provide the rotated secret in GitHub Actions secrets as well
as Vercel if running benchmarks there. Paid benchmarks are manual only. The vision
adapter remains Anthropic-specific; this release does not advertise OpenRouter
vision or Google Voice account synchronization.

## Verification

Unit/component tests cover multi-speaker finals, interim replacement, unknown
labels, separate-channel names, account-local export context, consent, tab-only
selection, sharing without audio, Stop/late grant cleanup, route auth, allowlisted
model preferences and complete/error/truncated provider responses. Provider/audio
responses in unit tests are fixtures, not live accuracy measurements.

Browser checks use the existing development-only preview mode, synthetic/no user
data and no live calls. Production auth remains protected. A physical Google Voice
call with at least two remote speakers and real microphones, and paid live-model
comparisons, are separate acceptance checks and must not be inferred from CI.

Sources checked for this release:
- https://support.google.com/voice/answer/3379129?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getDisplayMedia
- https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/diarization
- https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/streaming/label-speakers-and-separate-channels
- https://openrouter.ai/docs/quickstart
